written.headline: China's top tech firms face growing financial gap in AI build-out
written.summary: China's biggest tech companies are set to double their AI infrastructure capital expenditure to $139bn in 2026, according to a Rhodium Group report. Revenue from their AI labs covers less than 8% of this spending, highlighting broader financing pressures alongside US chip curbs.

written.headline: Databricks in early talks for funding at ~$225B valuation
written.summary: Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars at a valuation of about $225 billion. The potential new round follows a $5 billion funding round in August that valued the company at $190 billion.

written.headline: Cursor considers phasing out Chinese open-weight AI models due to geopolitical risk
written.summary: Cursor is considering phasing out Chinese open-weight AI models due to geopolitical risk, according to a congressional report. The SpaceX-owned coding platform previously built its Composer 2 model on Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5.

written.headline: SpaceX lenders reportedly seek to keep financed AI chips on Earth
written.summary: Lenders backing SpaceX's multibillion-dollar chip financing deal reportedly requested that the purchased hardware remain on Earth rather than being deployed to orbital data centers. Traditional asset-backed lending relies on the ability to seize and resell physical collateral if a borrower defaults.

written.headline: Ethan Mollick: AI models cannot yet solve complex problems alone
written.summary: Ethan Mollick stated that combining human expertise with AI enables people to accomplish remarkable tasks, as current models cannot operate independently. He noted that mathematicians solving Millennium Problems rely on human skill because models cannot yet do it all on their own.

written.headline: Google announces $5M funding for IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research
written.summary: Google announced $5 million in funding for IIT Kharagpur to accelerate advanced AI research and educational opportunities. The commitment will support research across Indic languages, materials science, agriculture, and educational technology.
